newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli president to make landmark India trip.
newsitem.headline: Israeli president to make landmark India trip.

text.p: President Ezer Weizman begins a groundbreaking visit to India on Sunday that officials say reflects Israel's growing ties with the world's most populous countries in Asia.
"It is a very important visit. It will be the first time the president of Israel visits India," said Israeli foreign ministry director-general Eytan Bentsur.
Ministry spokesman Yigal Palmor said the one-week visit should have an impact on the whole region given India's size and influence.
India and Israel forged relations in 1992 after Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat endorsed the move on a visit to New Delhi.
Israeli officials expect at least three agreements to be signed on cultural ties, trade and commerce during Weizman's visit. Senior Israeli industrialists were likely to join him.

Several Asian countries with traditional pro-Arab stands, including China, Vietnam and India, established ties with Israel after the Jewish state and its Arab neighbours took part in the first Middle East peace conference in Madrid in 1991.
Israeli officials say economic and cultural ties have been growing since. Bilateral trade stood at $600 million in 1995, said an Israeli diplomat in New Delhi.
Israeli media recently reported Israel was trying to sell naval vessels to India.
Many Israelis in their early 20s travel to India and East Asia on holiday after completing compulsory military service.

Asia's Islamic nations remain reluctant to establish formal ties with Israel. Israel has no official relations with any of Asia's Islamic nations though it maintains some contacts with Indonesia and Malaysia.
Then prime minister Yitzhak Rabin made a surprise unofficial stop in Indonesia, Islam's most populous country, while returning from China in 1993.
Israeli officials say Pakistan and Bangladesh have yet to show any interest in future links with the Jewish state.

Weizman's visit to India will be an emotional return to the country where he served as a British air force pilot some 50 years ago, Israeli officials say. He plans to visit the former British air base in the southern city of Bangalore, where he was stationed after World War Two.
